sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Mission, TX?
sections.html: Yes. Mission homes can sell to cash buyers, investors or on the open market, and sellers often choose cash when they inherit a house, move out of the Rio Grande Valley or want to avoid repair bills. Gather your deed and tax bill first and the process moves faster.

sections.h2: What is Mission, Texas known for?
sections.html:
Mission is a Hidalgo County city on the Rio Grande, founded in 1908 when the Missouri Pacific Railroad set up a station near the center of a new development. It was named for La Lomita Chapel, and the city's history page says the population is approaching 70,000.

The city describes this area as the place where citrus was first planted in the Rio Grande Valley. The multimillion-dollar citrus industry is celebrated each year at the Texas Citrus Fiesta, each year. For a seller, that heritage is the backdrop to the local housing stock.

  • The historic La Lomita Mission still stands and draws visitors.
  • William Jennings Bryan built a winter home in Mission, and the area appears in Larry McMurtry's Lonesome Dove.
  • Land here began as Spanish porciones that ran about two-thirds of a mile along the river and 11 to 16 miles inland, a pattern recorded in county land records.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a Mission house quickly?
sections.html:
There are three main routes, each with different timing and cost.

  • Cash buyer. Good for as-is sales, inherited homes with clouded title, and houses with storm or roof damage.
  • Agent listing. Often brings more money for homes in good shape, with showings and buyer financing timelines.
  • Seller financing or lease option. Slower and regulated; a Texas contract for deed on a residence is covered by Property Code chapter 5 and gives the buyer a right to cancel.

Get every offer in writing and ask who pays title, recording and survey costs.

sections.h2: What does Mission require for building permits and repairs?
sections.html:
Mission's Inspections Division reviews permits for new buildings and checks compliance with minimum building codes. A permit is also required for any concrete or asphalt slab with a value of $100 or more, and mobile homes need permits.

Inspectors check foundation, plumbing, framing, mechanical, A/C, electrical, setbacks, sidewalks and buffering on new residences. Structures that existed before annexation are treated as grandfathered while they stay as they are, but expanding one requires a permit and brings zoning and setback rules into play. The division's phone is 956-580-8691 per the city page. Before you list, ask whether an addition, slab or carport was permitted, since open work can slow a buyer's lender.

sections.h2: How does the Hidalgo County Appraisal District affect a Mission sale?
sections.html:
Hidalgo CAD appraises Mission property and handles homestead and over-65 applications through an online portal. Its customer service line is 956-381-8466.

Statewide, appraisal notices for homesteads go out around April 1, and protests are due by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. A homestead's appraised value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year under the state cap. Ask the district which exemptions are on your account so you can tell a buyer what to expect after closing. The district's official site lists the portal and contact details.

sections.h2: What exemptions might a buyer claim?
sections.html:
A buyer who will live in the house can apply for a residence homestead exemption. School districts must give $140,000, and an additional $60,000 applies to owners 65 or older or disabled.

  • A buyer who purchases after January 1 may get the exemption for the rest of that year if the prior owner did not.
  • Disabled veterans receive between $5,000 and $12,000 depending on rating; a 100 percent rating can exempt the whole homestead.
  • Heirs not on the deed can apply with an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

Details are on the Comptroller exemptions page.

sections.h2: What if a Mission house has unpaid taxes or a tax sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become a lien that can be foreclosed. The Comptroller says a lien attaches every January 1 and lets a court seize property even if ownership has changed. Collectors can add court costs, and private attorneys under contract can add up to 20 percent.

If land was sold at a tax sale, redemption rights are narrow. For a homestead, the owner has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed, paying a premium of 25 percent in the first year or 50 percent in the second, plus costs. Other property has 180 days. Former owners have two years to claim excess proceeds. Ask the county tax office for a payoff and an itemized statement before you decide.

  • Over-65 or disabled homeowners may pay delinquent amounts in installments.
  • Some collectors allow plans of up to 36 months, required on a homestead.
  • A waiver of penalty and interest must be asked for in writing.

sections.h2: How does a Mission seller compare offers?
sections.html:
Line up each offer on the same terms. A high price with a long inspection period can net you less than a lower cash offer that closes promptly.

  • Price and whether it is as-is.
  • Closing date and who selects the title company.
  • Who pays title, recording and survey fees.
  • Earnest money and what happens to it if the buyer backs out.
  • Whether the buyer needs financing or an appraisal.

Ask for the final numbers on a closing statement. If anything looks unclear, ask the title company, not the buyer, to explain it.

sections.h2: How do liens, probate and foreclosure play out in Mission?
sections.html:
Liens and taxes are paid from your proceeds at closing. If the house was inherited, the title company will ask for court orders or recorded documents showing who can sign. A will must be probated within four years of death, and a small estate affidavit is limited to estates with non-homestead assets of $75,000 or less.

If you are behind on the mortgage, Texas foreclosures are usually nonjudicial public auctions held on the first Tuesday of a month, with notice at least 21 days ahead. After a sale, a deficiency suit must be filed within two years. Selling first can keep any equity in your hands. The State Law Library foreclosure guide explains the stages.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded for a Mission property?
sections.html: The county clerk records it where the land sits. The deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer. The 2023 clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per extra page, plus capped records fees; ask the clerk for the current schedule.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mission house with storm or roof damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers commonly buy damaged houses as-is, and the offer reflects the repair cost. Listing usually requires repairs for lender approval.

faqs.q: Does Mission require permits for slabs and additions?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a permit for any concrete or asphalt slab valued at $100 or more, and expansion of older structures needs a permit and brings zoning setbacks into play.
The Hidalgo County Appraisal District. You can reach customer service at 956-381-8466 or use its online portal for homestead and over-65 applications.

faqs.q: What if I inherited a Mission house?
faqs.a: You need proof of authority to sell, such as a muniment of title, administration, or a transfer on death deed. Probate a will within four years of death.

faqs.q: Can I stop a foreclosure by selling?
faqs.a: Yes, if you close before the auction. Texas gives 20 days to reinstate after the default notice and at least 21 days' notice of the sale.
